Auto-generated documentation from the autonomous harness.

This viewer renders feature documentation written by the harness's **documenter** role. Each time a feature's validator marks it `passed`, the documenter produces or updates a Starlight page describing what was built, how to use it, and which `VAL-*` claims it satisfies.

## How it works

1. **Worker** implements a feature and commits.
2. **Validator** runs the validation contract. If all claims pass, the feature status flips to `passed`.
3. **Documenter** runs, reads the diff and the contract, and writes to `<project>/docs/features/F-xxx.md`.
4. This viewer picks it up via a symlink into `src/content/docs/projects/<slug>/`.

## Projects

See the sidebar for per-project docs. Symlinks are wired up by `bin/docs-viewer.sh` at startup, so only projects that have a `docs/` directory will appear.

## This is a separate process

The docs viewer runs on its own port (default `4325`) and has no runtime dependency on the harness control UI, the Restart web app, or any specific project's dev server. Start it, stop it, run it on another machine — it only needs filesystem access to the project dirs.

Spin up the web and api services with a single docker compose command.

## Overview

The repository ships as a two-service stack: a Vite + React frontend at
`http://localhost:5173` and a FastAPI backend at `http://localhost:8900`.
`docker compose up --build` boots both; no host-side Node or Python install
is required to run the app.

## Usage

From the repo root:

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

Once the services are up:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8900/health
# {"ok":true}

curl -I http://localhost:5173/
# HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

A scripted probe that performs the same boot-and-check flow ships at
`scripts/test_bootstrap.sh`:

```bash
./scripts/test_bootstrap.sh
```

It brings the stack up, waits up to 90 s for each service, asserts the
responses, and tears everything down on exit.

## API / Interface

**Services defined in `docker-compose.yml`:**

| Service | Host port | Container image base | Entrypoint |
|---------|-----------|----------------------|------------|
| `api`   | 8900      | Python (FastAPI + uvicorn) | `uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8900` |
| `web`   | 5173      | `node:20-alpine` (Vite) | `vite --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5173` |

**HTTP endpoints available after boot:**

- `GET http://localhost:8900/health` → `200 {"ok": true}`
- `GET http://localhost:5173/` → `200` HTML containing `<div id="root">`

**Repository layout:**

```
apps/
  web/
    package.json
    src/
    e2e/
    vite.config.ts
    tsconfig.json
  api/
    main.py
    pyproject.toml
    tests/
docker-compose.yml
scripts/test_bootstrap.sh
```

The frontend exposes the backend URL to the browser via the
`VITE_API_BASE` environment variable (default `http://localhost:8900`).
The backend persists to a SQLite file whose path is configurable via
`SHEETS_DB_PATH` (default `/data/sheets.db`, backed by the `api-data`
named volume).

A virtualized 100-row by 26-column grid shell reachable at /sheet/<id>, with pinned row and column headers.

## Overview

The frontend now has a real route. Visit `/sheet/<id>` and you get a grid
laid out as rows `1..100` and columns `A..Z`, with the row header column
and column header row pinned while the body scrolls. The grid is
virtualized — only the cells near the current scroll position are in the
DOM.

## Usage

Start the stack and open any sheet id in a browser:

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

```
http://localhost:5173/sheet/newsheet
http://localhost:5173/sheet/anything-you-want
```

The `id` segment is freeform — it becomes the sheet identifier the app
will later persist against. Unmatched paths render a small "open a sheet
at `/sheet/<id>`" landing message.

Every cell in the viewport has a stable DOM ref you can target:

```ts
document.querySelector('[data-cell="A1"]');
document.querySelector('[data-cell="Z100"]'); // after scrolling to bottom-right
```

## API / Interface

**Route**

| Path           | Component          | Notes                                 |
|----------------|--------------------|---------------------------------------|
| `/sheet/:id`   | `SheetPage`        | `:id` is URL-decoded, no slash allowed |
| anything else  | fallback landing   | `data-route="not-found"`               |

Routing is handled by a single regex in `apps/web/src/routing.ts`:

```ts
import { parseRoute } from "./routing";

parseRoute("/sheet/newsheet");
// { kind: "sheet", id: "newsheet" }

parseRoute("/nope");
// { kind: "not-found", path: "/nope" }
```

**Grid constants** (`apps/web/src/grid/constants.ts`)

| Name                | Value | Meaning                         |
|---------------------|------:|---------------------------------|
| `ROW_COUNT`         | 100   | Rows addressable (`1..100`)     |
| `COL_COUNT`         | 26    | Columns addressable (`A..Z`)    |
| `ROW_HEIGHT`        | 28 px | Body row height                 |
| `COL_WIDTH`         | 120 px| Body column width               |
| `ROW_HEADER_WIDTH`  | 48 px | Pinned row header column        |
| `COL_HEADER_HEIGHT` | 28 px | Pinned column header row        |

Helpers exported alongside:

```ts
columnLabel(0);   // "A"
columnLabel(25);  // "Z"
cellRef(0, 0);    // "A1"
cellRef(99, 25);  // "Z100"
```

**DOM contract** (stable selectors the rest of Phase 1 builds on)

- `[data-grid-root]` — outermost grid container
- `[data-grid-body]` — scrollable body (receives `scroll` events)
- `[data-grid-col-headers]` / `[data-grid-row-headers]` — pinned strips
- `[data-col-header="A"]` … `[data-col-header="Z"]`
- `[data-row-header="1"]` … `[data-row-header="100"]`
- `[data-cell="A1"]` … `[data-cell="Z100"]` — cells currently in the DOM

Virtualization uses `@tanstack/react-virtual` on both axes with
`overscan: 2`, which keeps the cell-node count ≤ 500 at the default
viewport.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-GRID-001** — `/sheet/<id>` renders the grid shell with column headers `A` and `Z` and row header `1` present.
- **VAL-GRID-002** — Grid is addressable across exactly 100 rows and 26 columns; row `100` and column `Z` are reachable, row `101` and column `AA` do not exist.
- **VAL-GRID-003** — Grid is virtualized: at any scroll position, `document.querySelectorAll('[data-cell]').length` stays ≤ 500, and off-screen cells (e.g. `A1` when scrolled to row 100) are absent from the DOM.
- **VAL-GRID-004** — Row and column headers stay pinned: column headers stay visible during vertical scroll, row headers stay visible during horizontal scroll (both implemented via `translateX/Y` synced to the body's scroll position).

## See also

- [F-001](/features/F-001/) — stack bootstrap (`docker compose up`) that serves this route.
- [F-002](/features/F-002/) — backend sheet store that the `:id` segment will eventually map to.

Click a cell to select it, move the selection with arrow keys, and use Tab / Shift+Tab to step across the row.

## Overview

A cell in the grid can now be selected. Clicking paints a 2px blue outline
on that cell, and the keyboard takes over from there: the arrow keys move
the selection up / down / left / right, Tab / Shift+Tab step across the
row, and Enter steps down. The selection is clamped to the A1..Z100 range
— there is no wrap-around at the edges.

## Usage

Open any sheet and click a cell:

```
http://localhost:5173/sheet/newsheet
```

1. Click `C5`. A blue outline appears around it.
2. Press `ArrowRight` → `D5` is now selected.
3. Press `ArrowDown` → `D6`. `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowUp` work symmetrically.
4. Press `Tab` → selection moves one column right. `Shift+Tab` moves it
   one column left.
5. Press `Enter` on an empty cell, then `Enter` again — selection moves
   down one row.

The selection also auto-scrolls into view: if you arrow past the bottom
of the visible area, the grid scrolls just enough to keep the selected
cell on screen.

You can query the currently selected cell from the DOM:

```ts
document.querySelector('[data-selected="true"]');
// → the single selected cell, e.g. <div data-cell="C5" data-selected="true" …>
```

## API / Interface

**Selection store** (`apps/web/src/store/useSheetStore.ts`) — a Zustand
store holds the grid's interaction state:

```ts
import { useSheetStore } from "./store/useSheetStore";

const {
  selectedCell,      // e.g. "C5" or null
  editingCell,       // e.g. "C5" while editing, else null
  selectCell,        // (ref: string | null) => void
} = useSheetStore();
```

**Key bindings** (grid-root handler, not-editing state):

| Key              | Effect                                        |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Click            | Select the clicked cell                       |
| `ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right` | Move selection one cell; clamped at edges |
| `Tab`            | Move selection one column right (clamped)     |
| `Shift+Tab`      | Move selection one column left (clamped)      |
| `Enter` / `F2`   | Enter edit mode on the selected cell          |
| Printable ASCII  | Enter edit mode with that character as value  |

**DOM contract** (extends the grid contract from F-003):

- The selected cell carries `data-selected="true"`. At most one cell on
  the page carries this attribute.
- Computed `outline-width` on the selected cell is non-zero (`2px solid
  #1a73e8`).
- The grid root (`[data-grid-root]`) is `tabIndex={0}` and owns keyboard
  focus while not editing.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-SEL-001** — Clicking `[data-cell="C5"]` sets `data-selected="true"`
  on that cell with a non-zero `outline-width`; no other cell carries the
  attribute.
- **VAL-SEL-002** — From `A1`, `ArrowRight`/`ArrowDown`/`ArrowLeft`/`ArrowUp`
  walk the selection through `B1 → B2 → A2 → A1`; at the top-left edge,
  further `ArrowUp`/`ArrowLeft` leave selection on `A1` without wrapping
  or throwing.
- **VAL-SEL-003** — Pressing `Enter` on a selected empty `A1` enters edit
  mode; a second `Enter` commits the (empty) edit and moves the selection
  to `A2`.
- **VAL-SEL-004** — Typing `x` on `A1` enters overwrite-edit; `Tab` commits
  `x` into `A1` and selects `B1`; `Shift+Tab` moves the selection back to
  `A1`.

Enter edit mode by typing, F2, Enter, or double-click; commit with Enter or Tab; cancel with Esc.

## Overview

A selected cell can now be edited. Typing a character overwrites the cell,
`F2` or `Enter` opens edit mode with the current value preserved, and a
double-click does the same with the mouse. Pressing `Enter` commits and
moves the selection down, `Tab` commits and moves right, and `Esc`
cancels the edit and restores the prior value.

## Usage

Open any sheet and click a cell to select it:

```
http://localhost:5173/sheet/newsheet
```

Four ways to enter edit mode on the selected cell:

1. **Type any printable character** (e.g. `5`) — replaces the cell's
   content with that character and opens the editor.
2. **Press `F2`** — opens the editor with the existing value, cursor at
   the end.
3. **Press `Enter`** — same as `F2`.
4. **Double-click the cell** — same as `F2`, driven from the mouse.

Three ways to leave edit mode:

- **`Enter`** — commits the new value; selection moves down one row.
- **`Tab`** / **`Shift+Tab`** — commits; selection moves one column right
  (or left).
- **`Esc`** — cancels; the cell keeps its prior value and selection stays
  put.

Clicking another cell while editing also commits, then moves the selection
to the clicked cell.

## API / Interface

**Store actions** (`apps/web/src/store/useSheetStore.ts`) — edit mode is
driven by three Zustand actions:

```ts
import { useSheetStore } from "./store/useSheetStore";

const {
  editingCell,    // ref currently being edited, or null
  editValue,      // the in-flight editor string
  startEdit,      // (ref, initialValue?) => void
  commitEdit,     // () => void — writes editValue into cells[editingCell]
  cancelEdit,     // () => void — discards editValue, clears editingCell
  setEditValue,   // (value: string) => void
} = useSheetStore();
```

- `startEdit(ref)` opens the editor with the cell's existing value
  (`F2` / `Enter` / double-click).
- `startEdit(ref, char)` opens it with `char` as the value
  (type-to-overwrite).
- Committing an empty string deletes the cell from the map.
- Cancelling keeps the cell's prior value and leaves selection on the
  edited cell.

**Key bindings**

| Context        | Key                 | Effect                                          |
|----------------|---------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| Not editing    | `F2` / `Enter`      | Enter edit mode; existing value preserved       |
| Not editing    | Printable ASCII     | Enter edit mode; value replaced with that char  |
| Not editing    | Double-click cell   | Enter edit mode; existing value preserved       |
| Editing        | `Enter`             | Commit; move selection down one row             |
| Editing        | `Tab`               | Commit; move selection one column right         |
| Editing        | `Shift+Tab`         | Commit; move selection one column left          |
| Editing        | `Esc`               | Cancel; restore prior value, stay on cell       |

**DOM contract**

- While editing, a single `<input>` element is present in the grid — it
  owns keyboard focus and its value mirrors `editValue`.
- When edit mode exits, the input is removed from the DOM and focus
  returns to `[data-grid-root]`.
- Printable-character detection uses the regex `/^[\x20-\x7E]$/` and
  ignores keys with `ctrlKey`, `metaKey`, or `altKey` modifiers.

Numbers, strings, and booleans flow through the hyperformula engine and render with type-appropriate alignment.

## Overview

Cell contents are no longer treated as opaque strings. When a value is
committed it passes through hyperformula, which classifies it as a number,
boolean, string, or error. Numbers render right-aligned; strings render
left-aligned; `TRUE` / `FALSE` become first-class booleans usable by
logical formulas like `=NOT()` and `=AND()`.

## Usage

Open a fresh sheet:

```
http://localhost:5173/sheet/newsheet
```

Type different kinds of values and watch the alignment and formulas
respond to type:

1. Select `A1`, type `42`, press `Enter`. A1 renders `42` right-aligned
   (`data-cell-type="number"`).
2. Select `A2`, type `hello`, press `Enter`. A2 renders `hello`
   left-aligned (`data-cell-type="string"`).
3. Select `A3`, type `TRUE`, press `Enter`. A3 renders `TRUE`
   (`data-cell-type="boolean"`).
4. Select `A4`, type `=NOT(A3)`, press `Enter`. A4 renders `FALSE`.
5. Select `A5`, type `=AND(A3, TRUE)`, press `Enter`. A5 renders `TRUE`.

Negative numbers (`-5`) and floats (`3.14`) are also recognized as
numbers.

## API / Interface

**Formula engine module** (`apps/web/src/engine/formulaEngine.ts`) —
thin facade over a single hyperformula instance:

```ts
import { setCellRaw, getCellRenderInfo } from "./engine/formulaEngine";

setCellRaw("A1", "42");          // number
setCellRaw("A2", "hello");       // string
setCellRaw("A3", "TRUE");        // boolean
setCellRaw("A4", "=NOT(A3)");    // formula
setCellRaw("A5", null);          // clear

const info = getCellRenderInfo("A1");
// { display: "42", kind: "number" }
```

- `setCellRaw(ref, raw)` — writes a cell. Coercion rules on `raw`:
  - starts with `=` → formula (with bare `TRUE` / `FALSE` normalized to
    `TRUE()` / `FALSE()` for hyperformula 2.x).
  - `TRUE` / `FALSE` (case-insensitive, trimmed) → boolean.
  - Parses as a number (`Number(raw)` finite) → number.
  - Otherwise → string.
  - `null` or empty string → cell cleared.
- `getCellRenderInfo(ref)` returns `{ display, kind }`:

  ```ts
  type CellValueKind =
    | "number" | "boolean" | "string" | "error" | "empty";

  interface CellRenderInfo {
    display: string;      // the text to paint in the cell
    kind: CellValueKind;  // the value type hyperformula reports
  }
  ```

**DOM contract** (extends F-003 / F-005):

- Every rendered cell carries `data-cell-type="<kind>"` where `<kind>`
  is one of `number`, `boolean`, `string`, `error`, `empty`.
- `data-cell-type="number"` cells have computed `text-align: right`; all
  others are `text-align: left`.
- The cell's visible text is `display`, not the raw entry — so
  `=NOT(TRUE)` shows as `FALSE`, and `=1+2` shows as `3`.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-VAL-001** — Entering `42` in A1 and `hello` in A2 produces a
  right-aligned `A1` with `data-cell-type="number"` and a left-aligned
  `A2` with `data-cell-type="string"`.
- **VAL-VAL-002** — Entering `TRUE` in A1 yields `data-cell-type="boolean"`;
  `=NOT(A1)` in A2 renders `FALSE`; `=AND(A1, TRUE)` in A3 renders
  `TRUE`.

## Limitations

- Type is not persisted to the server yet; a reload re-parses the raw
  string through the same coercion rules, so stable inputs round-trip
  to the same type but the server sees only strings. Full persistence
  of formula text lands in F-011.
- The grid still stores raw entry strings in its zustand `cells` map
  alongside hyperformula; the engine is the source of truth for
  display, the store is the source of truth for the editor buffer.
- Dot-delimited inputs like `1.2.3` were originally coerced to date
  serials by hyperformula's parser — see [F-FIX-016](/features/F-FIX-016/)
  for the patched behaviour.

Cells starting with `=` are evaluated by hyperformula — arithmetic, cell references, SUM ranges, absolute refs, and operator precedence all work, with live recalc under 200 ms.

## Overview

A cell whose value begins with `=` is now a formula. The hyperformula
engine evaluates it and the grid renders the result. Changing a
referenced cell recalculates every dependent cell synchronously, well
within 200 ms for the patterns Phase 1 cares about: arithmetic, SUM
over a range, absolute (`$A$1`) references, and operator precedence
including `^`, `*`, `/`, `+`, `-`, and parentheses.

## Usage

Open any sheet:

```
http://localhost:5173/sheet/newsheet
```

Enter values and formulas:

1. Select `A1`, type `10`, press `Enter`.
2. Select `A2`, type `20`, press `Enter`.
3. Select `A3`, type `=A1+A2`, press `Enter` — `A3` renders `30`.
4. Go back to `A1`, press `F2`, change to `5`, press `Enter` — `A3`
   updates to `25` within 200 ms.

Other supported shapes:

```
A1 = 10
A2 = 15
A3 = =SUM(A1:A2)         → 25;  change A2 to 100, A3 becomes 110

A1 = 7
B1 = =$A$1+1             → 8;   change A1 to 10, B1 becomes 11

A1 = =2^3                → 8
A2 = =(1+2)*3            → 9
A3 = =1+2*3              → 7
```

## API / Interface

The engine lives in `apps/web/src/engine/formulaEngine.ts` — a thin
facade over a single hyperformula instance:

```ts
import { setCellRaw, getCellRenderInfo } from "./engine/formulaEngine";

setCellRaw("A1", "10");
setCellRaw("A2", "20");
setCellRaw("A3", "=A1+A2");

getCellRenderInfo("A3");
// { display: "30", kind: "number" }
```

Formula-specific behavior:

- Any raw value starting with `=` is parsed as a formula. Bare
  `TRUE` / `FALSE` constants inside the formula are rewritten to
  `TRUE()` / `FALSE()` before handoff (hyperformula 2.x requires the
  function form).
- Relative (`A1`) and absolute (`$A$1`) references both resolve to the
  same cell for single-cell evaluation; the `$` markers only matter
  once copy/paste relative-adjustment lands (F-012).
- Range references (`A1:A2`) are accepted by the aggregate functions
  wired through hyperformula, e.g. `SUM`.
- Operator precedence follows the usual spreadsheet rules
  (`^` > `*` / `/` > `+` / `-`, with parentheses overriding).
- Recalc is synchronous: `setCellRaw` updates every dependent cell in
  the same call, so `getCellRenderInfo` on a downstream cell reflects
  the new value on the next render tick.

Errors returned from hyperformula (`#DIV/0!`, `#NAME?`, `#REF!`,
`#VALUE!`, `#CYCLE!`, `#NUM!`, `#N/A`) are mapped to their literal
display strings by `errorToString`, ready for the error-rendering work
in F-010.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-FORM-001** — `A1=10`, `A2=20`, `A3=\=A1+A2` renders `30`;
  changing `A1` to `5` updates `A3` to `25` within 200 ms.
- **VAL-FORM-003** — `A3=\=SUM(A1:A2)` over `A1=10`, `A2=15` renders
  `25`; changing `A2` to `100` updates `A3` to `110` within 200 ms.
- **VAL-FORM-005** — `B1=\=$A$1+1` over `A1=7` renders `8`; changing
  `A1` to `10` updates `B1` to `11` within 200 ms.
- **VAL-FORM-006** — `=2^3` renders `8`, `=(1+2)*3` renders `9`,
  `=1+2*3` renders `7`.

## Limitations

- Transitive recalc across chains of length > 1 is exercised by F-008,
  not here. Single-hop dependency updates are what this feature
  guarantees.
- The broader Phase-1 function library (`AVERAGE`, `IF`, `CONCAT`,
  `ROUND`, `TODAY`, …) is covered by F-009. The engine supports them
  because it is hyperformula, but they are not validated by this
  feature.
- Error rendering beyond the happy path is F-010's responsibility.

Changing a cell updates the whole chain of cells that depend on it — direct, indirect, multi-hop — within the 200 ms budget.

## Overview

When you edit a cell, every formula that references it recalculates —
and so does every formula that references *those* cells, and so on.
The grid reaches a consistent final state in a single synchronous pass,
regardless of chain depth. A 20-deep dependency chain repaints to its
correct final value within 200 ms.

## Usage

Open any sheet:

```
http://localhost:5173/sheet/newsheet
```

Build a three-hop chain and watch it propagate:

1. Select `A1`, type `1`, press `Enter`.
2. Select `B1`, type `=A1*2`, press `Enter` — `B1` renders `2`.
3. Select `C1`, type `=B1*2`, press `Enter` — `C1` renders `4`.
4. Re-select `A1`, press `F2`, change to `5`, press `Enter`. Within
   200 ms: `B1` renders `10`, `C1` renders `20`.

Deep chains behave the same:

```
A1  = 1
A2  = =A1+1    → 2
A3  = =A2+1    → 3
...
A20 = =A19+1   → 20

Change A1 to 100 → A20 renders 119 within 200 ms.
```

## API / Interface

Transitive recalc is a property of the existing engine facade, not a
new surface. Every `setCellRaw` call triggers the full recalc:

```ts
import { setCellRaw, getCellRenderInfo } from "./engine/formulaEngine";

setCellRaw("A1", "1");
setCellRaw("B1", "=A1*2");
setCellRaw("C1", "=B1*2");

setCellRaw("A1", "5");
getCellRenderInfo("B1"); // { display: "10", kind: "number" }
getCellRenderInfo("C1"); // { display: "20", kind: "number" }
```

- `setCellRaw` delegates to `hf.setCellContents` (see
  `apps/web/src/engine/formulaEngine.ts:71`). HyperFormula computes the
  dependency graph and walks it in topological order in the same call,
  so `getCellRenderInfo` on any dependent returns the post-change value
  on the next render tick.
- There is no async queue, no debounce, no partial state. Either a cell
  reads its old value or it reads its new one — intermediate states
  where `B1` has updated but `C1` has not are not observable to React.
- Cycles do not hang this path: they surface as `#CYCLE!` (see F-010).

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-FORM-002** — `A1=1`, `B1=\=A1*2`, `C1=\=B1*2`. Changing `A1` to
  `5` updates both `B1` to `10` AND `C1` to `20` within 200 ms.
- **VAL-PERF-003** — 20-deep chain (`A1=1`, `A2=\=A1+1`, …,
  `A20=\=A19+1`). Changing `A1` to `100` updates `A20` to `119` within
  200 ms.

  at depth.
- [F-006](/features/F-006/) — value-type pipeline that feeds the engine.

## Overview

The formula engine now supports the full Phase-1 function set: aggregate
math (`AVERAGE`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `SUM`, `COUNT`, `COUNTA`), logic (`IF`,
`AND`, `OR`, `NOT`), text (`CONCAT`, `LEN`, `UPPER`, `LOWER`, `TRIM`),
numeric (`ROUND`, `ABS`, `SQRT`), and date (`TODAY`, `NOW`). `CONCAT` is
accepted as an alias for `CONCATENATE`, and `TODAY()` / `NOW()` render
as formatted date strings rather than raw serial numbers.

## Usage

Open any sheet and try each function in a fresh cell:

```

A2  = =MIN(3,1,2)          → 1
A3  = =MAX(3,1,2)          → 3
A4  = =COUNT(1,"x",2)      → 2
A5  = =COUNTA(1,"x",2)     → 3
A6  = =IF(1>0,"yes","no")  → yes
A7  = =AND(TRUE,TRUE)      → TRUE
A8  = =OR(FALSE,TRUE)      → TRUE
A9  = =NOT(TRUE)           → FALSE
A10 = =CONCAT("a","b")     → ab
A11 = =LEN("abcd")         → 4
A12 = =UPPER("ab")         → AB
A13 = =LOWER("AB")         → ab
A14 = =TRIM("  x  ")       → x
A15 = =ROUND(1.567,1)      → 1.6
A16 = =ABS(-3)             → 3
A17 = =SQRT(9)             → 3
A18 = =TODAY()             → 2026-04-24
A19 = =NOW()               → 2026-04-24 14:07:33
```

## API / Interface

All functions route through the existing engine facade — no new public
surface:

```ts

setCellRaw("A1", "=CONCAT(\"a\",\"b\")");
getCellRenderInfo("A1"); // { display: "ab", kind: "string" }

setCellRaw("A2", "=TODAY()");
getCellRenderInfo("A2"); // { display: "2026-04-24", kind: "string" }
```

  the serial is converted via `hf.numberToDate` / `hf.numberToDateTime`
  and formatted as `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. The result is
  returned with `kind: "string"` so it renders left-aligned.

Formula errors render as the standard spreadsheet literals — `#DIV/0!`, `#NAME?`, `#CYCLE!`, `#REF!`, and `#VALUE!` — with a dedicated `error` cell kind.

## Overview

A formula that fails to evaluate now surfaces a recognisable error literal
in the cell rather than a raw engine error object. The five errors a
Phase-1 user can trigger — division by zero, unknown function name, direct
or indirect cycle, out-of-range reference, and type mismatch — each render
as their canonical string, and the cell is tagged with
`data-cell-type="error"` so downstream styling or assertions can target
error cells specifically.

## Usage

Type any of these into an empty cell to see the corresponding error:

```
=1/0        → #DIV/0!
=FOO()      → #NAME?
=A1         (entered in A1)        → #CYCLE!
=B1, =A1    (entered in A1 and B1) → #CYCLE! in both
=AA1        → #REF!   (AA is past the Z column)
=A101       → #REF!   (row 101 is past the 100-row limit)
```

And a type mismatch:

```
A1 = abc
A2 = =A1+1  → #VALUE!
```

## API / Interface

The engine facade `apps/web/src/engine/formulaEngine.ts` exposes a single
`CellRenderInfo` shape with an `error` kind:

```ts
export type CellValueKind =
  | "number"
  | "boolean"
  | "string"
  | "error"
  | "empty";

export interface CellRenderInfo {
  display: string;
  kind: CellValueKind;
}

export function getCellRenderInfo(ref: string): CellRenderInfo;
```

For an error cell, `display` is the literal token (e.g. `"#DIV/0!"`) and
`kind` is `"error"`. The grid renders this with
`data-cell-type="error"` on the cell element.

HyperFormula's native error codes are mapped to the Phase-1 literal set
in `errorToString`:

| HyperFormula `ErrorType` | Rendered literal |
|--------------------------|------------------|
| `DIV_BY_ZERO`            | `#DIV/0!`        |
| `NAME`                   | `#NAME?`         |
| `CYCLE`                  | `#CYCLE!`        |
| `REF`                    | `#REF!`          |
| `VALUE`                  | `#VALUE!`        |
| `NUM`                    | `#NUM!`          |
| `NA`                     | `#N/A`           |
| (fallback)               | `#ERROR!`        |

### Out-of-range reference detection

HyperFormula's lexer treats a multi-letter column reference such as `AA1`
as a function call when the column is beyond the configured sheet width,
which would otherwise surface as `#NAME?`. To produce the correct `#REF!`
for this grid's 26-column × 100-row limit, `setCellRaw` keeps the raw
formula string in a module-level `Map`, and `getCellRenderInfo` scans it
for any `[A-Z]+<row>` reference where the column is longer than one
letter or the row falls outside `1..100`, short-circuiting to
`{ display: "#REF!", kind: "error" }` before delegating to HyperFormula.
Function calls (identifiers immediately followed by `(`) are skipped so
`=SUM(...)` and similar are not misclassified.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-ERR-001** — `=1/0` renders exactly `#DIV/0!`.
- **VAL-ERR-002** — `=FOO()` (unknown function) renders exactly `#NAME?`.
- **VAL-ERR-003** — A self-reference `A1 = =A1` renders exactly `#CYCLE!`.
- **VAL-ERR-004** — An indirect cycle `A1 = =B1` / `B1 = =A1` renders
  `#CYCLE!` in both participating cells.
- **VAL-ERR-005** — Both `=AA1` (column beyond Z) and `=A101` (row beyond
  100) render exactly `#REF!`.
- **VAL-ERR-006** — `A1 = abc`, `A2 = =A1+1` renders `#VALUE!` in A2.

## Limitations

- Only the five Phase-1 errors above are explicitly covered by the
  validation contract. `#NUM!`, `#N/A`, and the generic `#ERROR!`
  fallback are implemented but not independently tested.
- The out-of-range check is grid-size-specific (hard-coded to 26 columns
  and 100 rows). If the grid dimensions change, `containsOutOfRangeRef`
  needs to change with them.

Client persistence — debounced save + hydrate on load
Sheet edits survive a page reload, formula text is preserved across the round-trip, and writes are debounced so typing does not hit the API per keystroke.

## Overview

Opening `/sheet/<id>` now hydrates the grid from the API, and subsequent
edits are written back automatically with a 500 ms debounce. Formulas are
persisted as their source text, so reloading a cell such as `=A1+A2`
restores the formula (not the evaluated number). Visiting a fresh sheet
id is not an error — the API returns an empty cell map and the grid
renders blank.

## Usage

The hook is wired into `SheetPage`, so any route that mounts that
component gets persistence for free:

```tsx
// apps/web/src/SheetPage.tsx
import { usePersistence } from "./hooks/usePersistence";

export function SheetPage({ sheetId }: SheetPageProps): JSX.Element {
  usePersistence(sheetId);
  return <Grid />;
}
```

Concrete click-path:

1. Navigate to `http://localhost:5173/sheet/demo`.
2. Type `42` in A1, press **Enter**.
3. Wait ≥ 500 ms (debounce window). A single `POST /api/sheet/demo`
   fires with `{"cells": {"A1": "42"}}`.
4. Reload the page. A1 still reads `42`.

Formula text preservation:

1. A1 = `5`, A2 = `10`, A3 = `=A1+A2`. A3 renders `15`.
2. Wait for the debounced save, then reload.
3. A3 still renders `15`. Select A3, press **F2** — the editor shows
   `=A1+A2`, not the literal `15`.

The API base URL is read from `import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE` and
defaults to `http://localhost:8900`.

## API / Interface

**Hook:**

```ts
// apps/web/src/hooks/usePersistence.ts
export function usePersistence(sheetId: string): void;
```

Mount this once at the top of a sheet view. It has two effects:
a one-shot hydrate on mount (and whenever `sheetId` changes), and a
debounced save that fires 500 ms after the Zustand `cells` Map changes.
The first `cells` update after hydration is skipped so the hydrate does
not immediately round-trip back to the server.

**HTTP client (`apps/web/src/api/sheetApi.ts`):**

```ts
export async function loadSheet(id: string): Promise<Record<string, string>>;
export async function saveSheet(
  id: string,
  cells: Record<string, string>,
): Promise<void>;
```

- `loadSheet` — `GET ${VITE_API_BASE}/api/sheet/${id}`. Returns the
  `cells` dict, or `{}` on a non-OK response.
- `saveSheet` — `POST ${VITE_API_BASE}/api/sheet/${id}` with body
  `{"cells": { ... }}`.

**Store action (`apps/web/src/store/useSheetStore.ts`):**

```ts
loadCells: (saved: Record<string, string>) => void;
```

Bulk-populates the Zustand `cells` Map and mirrors every entry into the
HyperFormula engine via `setCellRaw`, so formulas are re-parsed and
recalculated at hydrate time.

**Debounce behaviour:** typing into the edit buffer mutates only
`editValue` in the store; the `cells` Map is not touched until commit
(Enter / Tab / click-away). Because the save effect depends on `cells`,
no POST fires mid-typing — only one POST (500 ms after commit) for an
11-keystroke edit like `hello world`.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-PERSIST-001** — Entering `42` in A1, waiting ≥ 800 ms, and
  reloading `/sheet/persist-test` leaves A1 reading `42`.
- **VAL-PERSIST-002** — Formula text is persisted: `=A1+A2` in A3
  round-trips as `=A1+A2` (F2 after reload shows the formula, not `15`).
- **VAL-PERSIST-003** — Writes are debounced: typing `hello world` in
  A1 and committing produces ≤ 2 (typically 1) POSTs to `/api/sheet/*`
  within 2 s, with zero POSTs during the keystrokes themselves.
- **VAL-PERSIST-004** — Visiting `/sheet/<random-new-id>` renders the
  grid without an error banner or console error, and a subsequent edit
  becomes visible to `GET /api/sheet/<id>`.

## Limitations

- No save-status indicator in the UI — the 500 ms window is invisible
  to the user. (Edits committed inside that window are flushed on tab
  close / reload via `sendBeacon`; see [F-FIX-010](/features/F-FIX-010/).)
- No conflict resolution: a concurrent writer to the same sheet id
  will have its changes silently overwritten by the next debounced
  flush from this client.
- `loadSheet` swallows non-OK responses and returns `{}`, so a
  transient API outage on mount is indistinguishable from a brand-new
  sheet.

Clipboard copy/paste — single cell preserves formula text
Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V on a selected cell round-trips the raw formula or value through the system clipboard, not the evaluated result.

## Overview

Copying a cell now places its **source text** on the system clipboard —
the formula `=A1+A2`, not the rendered number `15`. Pasting writes that
same text into the selected cell, so a pasted formula is re-parsed and
re-evaluated at its new location instead of being frozen to its previous
value.

## Usage

Click-path:

1. In A1 enter `5`, in A2 enter `10`, in A3 enter `=A1+A2`. A3 renders
   `15`.
2. Click A3 to select it. Press **Ctrl+C** (or **Cmd+C** on macOS).
3. Click B3. Press **Ctrl+V**.
4. B3 renders `15` (HyperFormula re-evaluates `=A1+A2` in B3's context).
5. Press **F2** on B3 — the editor shows the formula (starts with `=`),
   not the literal `15`.

Plain values behave the same way: copying A1 = `hello` and pasting into
A2 yields A2 = `hello`, and F2 on A2 shows `hello` (no `=` prefix).

```ts
// What lands on the clipboard for a selected cell:
navigator.clipboard.readText(); // "=A1+A2"   — for a formula cell
navigator.clipboard.readText(); // "hello"    — for a plain-value cell
```

## API / Interface

**Keyboard (grid-level, cell selected, not in edit mode):**

- **Ctrl/Cmd+C** — reads the raw stored text for the selected cell
  (formula source or plain value) and calls
  `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)`.
- **Ctrl/Cmd+V** — calls `navigator.clipboard.readText()` and writes
  the result into the selected cell via `setCellDirect`.

Both handlers `preventDefault()` and no-op silently if the Clipboard
API rejects (e.g. permission denied).

**Store action (`apps/web/src/store/useSheetStore.ts`):**

```ts
setCellDirect: (ref: string, value: string) => void;
```

Writes `value` into the Zustand `cells` Map at `ref` and mirrors it
into HyperFormula via `setCellRaw`. Unlike the edit-commit path, this
does **not** go through edit mode — there is no `startEdit` /
`commitEdit` round-trip. An empty string deletes the cell. The action
also clears any dangling `editingCell` / `editValue`, so a paste while
an editor is open is safe.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-CLIP-001** — Copying a formula cell (`=A1+A2`) places the
  formula text on the clipboard (not the evaluated `15`); pasting into
  B3 makes B3 a formula cell whose F2 editor starts with `=`.
- **VAL-CLIP-003** — Copying a plain-value cell (`hello`) places
  `hello` on the clipboard; pasting into A2 makes A2 read `hello` with
  an F2 editor content of `hello` (no `=` prefix).

## Limitations

Pasting tab/newline-delimited clipboard text spreads it across a rectangular block anchored at the selected cell.

## Overview

Pasting text that contains tabs or newlines now expands into a rectangular
range of cells instead of dumping the whole blob into one cell. Rows are
split on newlines, columns on tabs, and the top-left of the paste lands
at the selected cell. This is the standard Sheets / Excel interop shape
for copying rectangular data out of other tools.

Single-cell paste (clipboard text with no `\t` or `\n`) is unchanged —
see [F-012](/features/F-012/).

## Usage

Click-path:

1. Put TSV text on the system clipboard, e.g. `"1\t2\n3\t4"` (copying a
   2×2 block out of another spreadsheet produces exactly this).
2. Click the anchor cell — say **A1**.
3. Press **Ctrl+V** (or **Cmd+V**).
4. A1=`1`, B1=`2`, A2=`3`, B2=`4`.

```ts
// Paste a 2×2 block anchored at A1
await navigator.clipboard.writeText("1\t2\n3\t4");
// focus A1, then Ctrl+V
// → A1=1, B1=2, A2=3, B2=4
```

The paste handler normalizes `\r\n` and bare `\r` to `\n` before splitting,
so clipboards from Windows / legacy Mac apps land in the right shape.
A trailing empty row (from clipboard text ending in a newline) is dropped
rather than clearing the row below the data. Cells that would land
outside the 100×26 grid are silently skipped; the in-bounds portion of
the paste still lands.

## API / Interface

**Keyboard (grid-level, cell selected, not in edit mode):**

- **Ctrl/Cmd+V** — calls `navigator.clipboard.readText()`. If the text
  contains no tab or newline, it is written into the selected cell via
  `setCellDirect` (the F-012 path). Otherwise the text is split by
  `\n` (rows) and `\t` (columns) and the resulting 2-D grid is written
  via `setCellsBatch`, with the top-left at the currently selected cell.

**Store action (`apps/web/src/store/useSheetStore.ts`):**

```ts
setCellsBatch: (batch: Record<string, string>) => void;
```

Writes every `ref → value` pair in `batch` into the Zustand `cells` Map
and mirrors each into HyperFormula via `setCellRaw`, in a single pass.
An empty-string value deletes the cell (same semantics as
`setCellDirect`). The action also clears any dangling `editingCell` /
`editValue`, so pasting while an editor is open is safe.

Preferring a batch action over a loop of `setCellDirect` calls keeps the
paste to one React render, which matters for larger TSV blocks.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-CLIP-002** — With `"1\t2\n3\t4"` on the clipboard and A1
  selected, Ctrl+V produces A1=`1`, B1=`2`, A2=`3`, B2=`4`.

## Limitations

- **Raw text only.** Values are written verbatim; a cell in the TSV
  that starts with `=` becomes a formula in the target, but there is no
  HTML or RTF clipboard handling (no styling, no merged cells, no
  number-format inheritance).
- **No relative-reference adjustment.** A formula pasted as part of a
  TSV block keeps its literal text — `=A1+A2` stays `=A1+A2` no matter
  where it lands.
- **Clips at the grid edge.** Cells beyond row 100 or column Z are
  dropped silently; no error or banner.

Performance budget — 100 rapid edits and 2600-cell first paint
The grid holds a measured performance budget: 100 back-to-back cell edits complete in under 5 s and a fully-populated 100×26 sheet first-paints in under 2 s.

## Overview

The grid now has a measured, test-enforced performance budget. A burst of
100 back-to-back cell edits (with commit between each) completes in well
under 5 s, and loading a sheet pre-populated with all 2600 cells paints
its first cell value in under 2 s. Both budgets are guarded by Playwright
specs that run against the normal dev server.

Under the hood this is a render-scope change: every visible cell used
to subscribe to the whole Zustand store, so any store update forced a
full re-render of every cell and editor. Cells and the inline editor are
now `React.memo` components driven by props, and the Grid subscribes only
to the few store slices that actually change its output.

## Usage

The budget is verified by `apps/web/e2e/performance.spec.ts`. Run it
against a live dev stack:

```bash
docker compose up --build -d
cd apps/web
npx playwright test e2e/performance.spec.ts
```

What the two tests do:

1. **100-edit burst** — navigates to `/sheet/perf-001-<ts>`, selects A1,
   then dispatches keydown + Enter pairs for values `"1"` through `"100"`
   inside a single `page.evaluate` so Playwright↔browser IPC stays out
   of the measurement. Asserts wall time < 5000 ms, reloads, and
   asserts A1/A50/A100 still render their values plus a
   `GET /api/sheet/<id>` round-trip that confirms every A1–A100 is
   persisted.
2. **2600-cell first paint** — seeds sheet `big` via
   `POST /api/sheet/big` with every cell A1..Z100 set, then measures
   `Date.now()` from `page.goto('/sheet/big')` until `[data-cell="A1"]`
   renders its seeded text. Asserts < 2000 ms.

Typical measured numbers on a developer laptop: the 100-edit burst
completes in a few hundred ms of browser time; the cold first paint on
the 2600-cell sheet lands around 400–600 ms against the 2000 ms budget.

## API / Interface

Two implementation surfaces changed to hit the budget.

**Bulk hydrate — `apps/web/src/engine/formulaEngine.ts`:**

```ts
// Batch-replaces every cell in the sheet in a single HyperFormula
// recalc pass.
export function loadAllCells(saved: Record<string, string>): void;
```

`loadCells` in the store now calls `loadAllCells`, which builds a
`100 × 26` `RawCellContent[][]` grid and hands it to
`hf.setSheetContent(sheetId, rows)`. HyperFormula does one topological
recalc over the whole sheet instead of 2600 individual
`setCellContents` calls. This is what fits the 2600-cell load under
the first-paint budget.

**Render scope — `apps/web/src/grid/Grid.tsx`:**

The Grid previously destructured the whole Zustand store
(`useSheetStore()`), so every commit invalidated it — and every visible
cell — in one notify. It now subscribes selectively:

```tsx
const selectedCell   = useSheetStore((s) => s.selectedCell);
const editingCell    = useSheetStore((s) => s.editingCell);
useSheetStore((s) => s.formulaVersion); // side-effect subscription
```

Visible cells are rendered via a memoized `GridCell` component that
takes its `display`, `kind`, `isSelected`, and `isEditing` as props —
no store subscription of its own. The input is a separate memoized
`InlineEditor` that owns the `editValue` / `setEditValue` subscription,
so keystrokes during edit mode do not re-render the Grid or any cell.

**Recalc signalling — `apps/web/src/store/useSheetStore.ts`:**

```ts
interface SheetState {
  // ...
  formulaVersion: number; // ++ on every commit that may change displays
}
```

`commitEdit`, `setCellDirect`, `setCellsBatch`, and `loadCells` each
increment `formulaVersion`. The Grid subscribes to it for its
side-effect (re-read cell render info), but individual cells do not —
`React.memo` skips any cell whose props are unchanged.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-PERF-001** — 100 distinct values typed into A1..A100 back-to-back
  with Enter between each complete in < 5 s; all 100 values survive a
  full page reload and are present in `GET /api/sheet/<id>`.
- **VAL-PERF-002** — A sheet seeded with all 2600 cells (A1..Z100)
  populated via the API first-paints A1 with its seeded value in
  < 2 s from navigation-start.

## Limitations

- The `VAL-PERF-001` spec dispatches key events inside `page.evaluate`
  rather than using Playwright's `page.keyboard.press`. This accurately
  exercises the React event path but does not probe the OS-level
  keyboard pipeline. A separate follow-up issue tracks a race that
  affects rapid physical typing.
- The 2000 ms first-paint budget is measured on the validator host;
  slower hardware or a cold Vite dev server will exceed it. The number
  is a CI guard, not a hardware-independent guarantee.

  depends on.

Build hygiene — tsc strict, mypy green, hyperformula locked in
The frontend builds clean under TypeScript strict mode, the backend passes strict mypy, and HyperFormula is the single pinned formula engine — all three gates are enforced by tests.

## Overview

The build gates that the rest of the project depends on are now green and
test-enforced. The frontend compiles with `"strict": true` and zero errors
under `tsc --noEmit`; the backend passes strict `mypy apps/api`; and
HyperFormula is the only formula engine in the tree, imported from
`apps/web/src` and pinned through the lockfile. A pytest module verifies
all three gates together, so a regression on any of them fails CI rather
than drifting silently.

## Usage

Run the full hygiene suite from the repo root:

```bash
# TypeScript strict — frontend
cd apps/web && npx tsc --noEmit

# mypy strict — backend
cd ../.. && mypy apps/api

# All three gates as pytest assertions
pytest apps/api/tests/test_build_hygiene.py
```

Expected: each command exits `0`, and the pytest module reports **7
passed**. The same checks run in `npm run build` (which chains
`tsc --noEmit && vite build`) and in the Docker build, so a broken gate
surfaces on the first container rebuild.

## API / Interface

Three surfaces are gated.

**Frontend TypeScript — `apps/web/tsconfig.json`:**

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,
    "noUnusedLocals": true,
    "noUnusedParameters": true,
    "noFallthroughCasesInSwitch": true
  },
  "include": ["src"]
}
```

`as any` / `as unknown as` escape hatches anywhere in `src`. The one
place that previously needed narrowing — HyperFormula's
`numberToDate` / `numberToDateTime` return a union of
`SimpleTime | SimpleDate | SimpleDateTime` — is handled with
in-operator guards in `apps/web/src/engine/formulaEngine.ts`:

```ts
  return { display: `${d.year}-${pad2(d.month)}-${pad2(d.day)}`, kind: "string" };

if ("year" in dt && "hours" in dt) {
  return {
    display: `${dt.year}-${pad2(dt.month)}-${pad2(dt.day)} ${pad2(dt.hours)}:${pad2(dt.minutes)}:${pad2(dt.seconds)}`,
    kind: "string",
  };
}
```

```toml
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
strict = true
files = ["main.py"]
```

Fixes the permanently-unhealthy web container by using the IPv4 loopback address in the Docker healthcheck.

## Overview

The `web` service defined in `docker-compose.yml` now passes its Docker
healthcheck. Previously the container was stuck reporting `unhealthy` even
though Vite was serving traffic on `http://localhost:5173/` from the host.
Tools that gate on container health — `docker compose up --wait`, downstream
`depends_on: condition: service_healthy`, CI smoke checks — now work
correctly.

## Usage

Bring the stack up and inspect the web container's health:

```bash
docker compose up --build -d
docker inspect --format '{{.State.Health.Status}}' sheets-clone-web
# healthy
```

`docker compose up --wait` now returns once the web container is healthy
instead of timing out.

## API / Interface

The change is one character in `docker-compose.yml`:

```yaml
web:
  healthcheck:
    test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -q -O /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:5173/ || exit 1"]
    interval: 5s
    timeout: 3s
    retries: 20
```

### Why `127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost`

Inside the `node:20-alpine` image, `/etc/hosts` lists `::1 localhost` before
`127.0.0.1 localhost`. BusyBox `wget` resolves `localhost` to `::1` first.
Vite is launched with `--host 0.0.0.0`, which only binds the IPv4 wildcard,
so the probe hit the unbound IPv6 loopback and returned
`wget: can't connect to remote host: Connection refused`. Using the explicit
IPv4 literal `127.0.0.1` bypasses name resolution entirely and matches the
address Vite is listening on.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-FIX-1 @ docker-compose.yml:34** — The web service healthcheck URL
  uses `http://127.0.0.1:5173/` and does not use `http://localhost:5173`.
  Enforced by `apps/api/tests/test_fix_001.py`:
  - `test_web_healthcheck_uses_ipv4_loopback` asserts `127.0.0.1:5173` is
    present in `docker-compose.yml`.
  - `test_web_healthcheck_does_not_use_bare_localhost` asserts
    `http://localhost:5173` is not present.

## See also

- [F-001](/features/F-001/) — docker-compose bootstrap that defines both services.

Adds a UTF-8 CSV export endpoint for sheets that no longer crashes on Korean, Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, or emoji cell values.

## Overview

The API now exposes a dedicated CSV export endpoint for any sheet. Cell
values containing non-ASCII text — Korean (`한국`), Chinese (`中文`), emoji
(`😀🎉`) — are written through as valid UTF-8 instead of returning HTTP
500. The response is a 100×26 CSV grid covering every addressable cell
(rows 1–100, columns A–Z); unset cells are emitted as empty fields.

## Usage

Export any sheet by GETting its `export.csv` subresource:

```bash
# Populate a sheet with unicode values
curl -X POST http://localhost:8900/api/sheet/demo \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"cells": {"A1": "한국", "B1": "中文", "C1": "😀"}}'

# Export it as CSV — response is UTF-8
curl -o demo.csv http://localhost:8900/api/sheet/demo/export.csv
head -1 demo.csv
# 한국,中文,😀,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,
```

The response sets `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<id>.csv"`,
so browsers and `curl -OJ` save it under the sheet's id.

## API / Interface

**`GET /api/sheet/{sheet_id}/export.csv`**

- **Response body:** CSV-encoded 100×26 grid of the sheet's cells, UTF-8.
- **Response headers:**
  - `content-type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`
  - `content-disposition: attachment; filename="{sheet_id}.csv"`
- **Status codes:**
  - `200` for known sheets.
  - `200` with an empty grid for sheet ids that have never been written.

Internally the grid is assembled by `cells_to_csv_bytes` in
`apps/api/exports/csv.py`, which uses `io.StringIO` + `csv.writer` +
`.encode("utf-8")` — no byte-mode file handle, no locale-dependent
encoding. References outside `A1:Z100` are ignored rather than resized
into.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-FIX-002 @ apps/api/exports/csv.py:67** — CSV export correctly
  handles unicode characters in cell values; exporting a sheet with
  Korean / Chinese / emoji text returns 200 and preserves the unicode
  exactly in the output. Enforced by
  `apps/api/tests/test_fix_002.py` (ASCII, Korean, Chinese, emoji, mixed,
  unknown-sheet, content-type, and UTF-8 validity cases).

## Limitations

- The URL path itself was originally parsed as latin-1 by Starlette's
  header builder, so a unicode `sheet_id` (e.g. `/api/sheet/한국/export.csv`)
  failed when building the `Content-Disposition` header. Cell values
  always round-tripped cleanly; the id-in-path case is now fixed in
  [F-FIX-015](/features/F-FIX-015/) via RFC 5987 pct-encoding.
- CSV formula injection (values beginning with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`) is
  not mitigated — consumers that open the file in Excel/Sheets should
  treat cells as data.
- A GET against a sheet id that was never created returns a `200` with
  an empty grid rather than `404`.

## See also

- [F-002](/features/F-002/) — FastAPI + SQLite sheet store the export reads from.

Adds idx_customers_email so WHERE email=? lookups on the 500k-row customers table complete in under 100 ms instead of ~1800 ms.

## Overview

The canonical schema for the API now lives at `apps/api/db/schema.sql` and
defines an index, `idx_customers_email`, on `customers(email)`. A single-
row lookup by email on a 500 000-row table drops from ~1 800 ms (full
scan) to well under 100 ms. The same file also holds the `sheets` table
DDL so every component — app code, tests, future migrations — refers to
one source of truth.

## Usage

Apply the schema to any fresh SQLite database and the index comes along
for the ride:

```bash
sqlite3 customers.db < apps/api/db/schema.sql

sqlite3 customers.db "EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT id, email, name
                      FROM customers WHERE email = 'user@example.com';"
# QUERY PLAN
# `--SEARCH customers USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_customers_1 (email=?)
```

The `SEARCH ... USING INDEX` line confirms the planner is using an index
rather than scanning the table.

## API / Interface

**`apps/api/db/schema.sql`** — the canonical DDL. Declares:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS customers (
    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    email      TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    name       TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    created_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_customers_email
    ON customers (email);
```

Apply it with `sqlite3 <db> < apps/api/db/schema.sql` or, from Python,
`connection.executescript(Path("apps/api/db/schema.sql").read_text())`.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-FIX-003 @ apps/api/db/schema.sql:42** — a `SELECT ... WHERE email = ?`
  against a 500 000-row `customers` table completes in under 100 ms,
  indicating an index is present and used. Verified by
  `apps/api/tests/test_fix_003.py` (5 tests): schema file exists,
  defines the `customers` table, defines `idx_customers_email`, the index
  is registered in `sqlite_master`, and the 500k-row timed lookup stays
  inside the 100 ms budget (validator measured mean 0.036 ms / max
  0.063 ms over 10 distinct lookups).

## Limitations

- `apps/api/main.py` does not run `schema.sql` on startup. Its
  `_connect()` creates the `sheets` table inline and never touches the
  `customers` table, so `idx_customers_email` only exists in databases
  that explicitly apply `schema.sql` (the pytest fixture does; a
  deployed API instance does not yet).
- Because `email` is declared `UNIQUE`, SQLite already creates an
  implicit `sqlite_autoindex_customers_1` covering the same column. The
  planner typically picks the autoindex over the explicit
  `idx_customers_email`; the explicit index is kept for clarity and to
  survive a future relaxation of the `UNIQUE` constraint.

## See also

- [F-002](/features/F-002/) — FastAPI + SQLite sheet store that shares
  `schema.sql` for the `sheets` table DDL.

Backup job fails loudly on full disk
The SQLite backup utility now raises DiskSpaceError with a logged ERROR when the target filesystem is more than 80% full, instead of failing silently.

## Overview

`apps/api/backup.py` provides a small CLI + library for copying the
sheets SQLite database into a backup directory. Before running the copy
it checks the destination filesystem and, if it is more than 80 % full,
refuses the backup — raising `DiskSpaceError` and logging an ERROR line
that names the directory and the measured usage percentage. Successful
runs log an INFO line naming the backup file.

## Usage

Run it against any SQLite database and target directory:

```bash
python apps/api/backup.py sheets.db /var/backups/sheets
# INFO Backup written to /var/backups/sheets/sheets.db
# OK: /var/backups/sheets/sheets.db
echo $?
# 0
```

When the target disk is too full the same command exits non-zero and
prints the reason:

```bash
python apps/api/backup.py sheets.db /var/backups/sheets
# ERROR Backup aborted: disk at '/var/backups/sheets' is 87.4% full (threshold 80%). Free space and retry.
echo $?
# 1
```

Or call it from Python:

```python
from apps.api.backup import DiskSpaceError, run_backup

try:
    dest = run_backup("sheets.db", "/var/backups/sheets")
except DiskSpaceError as exc:
    alert_oncall(str(exc))
```

## API / Interface

**`apps/api/backup.py`** exposes:

- **`run_backup(source_db, backup_dir, *, disk_threshold=0.80) -> Path`**
  Creates `backup_dir` if missing, checks its filesystem's
  `used / total` fraction, and — if the fraction is strictly greater
  than `disk_threshold` — raises `DiskSpaceError` after logging an
  ERROR. Otherwise copies `source_db` into `backup_dir` (preserving
  metadata via `shutil.copy2`), logs INFO, and returns the destination
  `Path`.
- **`DiskSpaceError(RuntimeError)`** — raised when a backup is aborted
  because the target disk is too full. The message contains the backup
  directory path and the usage percentage to one decimal place.
- **`DISK_FULL_THRESHOLD = 0.80`** — the module-level default threshold
  (80 %).
- **`main(argv=None) -> int`** — CLI entry point. Usage:
  `python backup.py <source_db> <backup_dir>`. Exits `0` on success,
  `1` on `DiskSpaceError`, `OSError`, or wrong argument count.

Threshold semantics: `fraction > threshold` fails. A fraction of
exactly `0.80` still succeeds.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-FIX-004 @ apps/api/backup.py:22** — the backup job handles
  disk-space constraints gracefully: when disk usage exceeds 80 % the
  run fails loudly with a `DiskSpaceError` whose message names the
  directory and percentage, and an ERROR-level log record is emitted
  (never a silent failure). Verified by `apps/api/tests/test_fix_004.py`
  (14 tests): disk-full raises, error message contains the percentage
  and path, ERROR log is captured, boundary at exactly 0.80 succeeds,
  0.801 fails, success path returns an existing path whose bytes match
  the source, backup directory is auto-created, INFO log is emitted on
  success, custom thresholds are honoured, and the CLI returns non-zero
  on disk-full / wrong arg count and zero on success.

## Limitations

- `backup.py` is a standalone script — it is not wired into the FastAPI
  app, `docker-compose.yml`, or any scheduler, so nothing runs it
  automatically yet. Operators must invoke it manually or from an
  external cron.
- There is no rotation. Each run overwrites the previous backup file of
  the same name in `backup_dir`.

## See also

- [F-FIX-011](/features/F-FIX-011/) — replaces the `shutil.copy2`
  copy step with `sqlite3.Connection.backup()` so the snapshot is
  consistent under concurrent writers and WAL mode.
- [F-002](/features/F-002/) — FastAPI + SQLite sheet store whose
  database file is what this utility backs up.

API CORS configured for the dev frontend
The FastAPI backend now mounts CORSMiddleware so that browser requests from http://localhost:5173 succeed instead of failing preflight with a 405 and missing Access-Control-Allow-Origin.

## Overview

`apps/api/main.py` registers Starlette's `CORSMiddleware` with
`allow_origins=["http://localhost:5173"]`, `allow_credentials=True`, and
wildcard methods / headers. Browsers running the Vite dev server at
`http://localhost:5173` can now issue `OPTIONS` preflights and
cross-origin `GET` / `POST` requests to the API at
`http://localhost:8900` and receive the expected
`Access-Control-Allow-*` response headers. Requests from other origins
are rejected (no wildcard ACAO leak).

## Usage

Preflight from the dev frontend now returns `200` with the CORS headers
filled in:

```bash
curl -i -X OPTIONS http://localhost:8900/api/sheet/demo \
  -H 'Origin: http://localhost:5173' \
  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' \
  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: content-type'
# HTTP/1.1 200 OK
# access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:5173
# access-control-allow-methods: *
# access-control-allow-headers: content-type
# access-control-allow-credentials: true
# vary: Origin
```

A real cross-origin `POST` succeeds and echoes the origin back:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8900/api/sheet/demo \
  -H 'Origin: http://localhost:5173' \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"cells": {"A1": "42"}}'
# HTTP/1.1 200 OK
# access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:5173
# access-control-allow-credentials: true
# vary: Origin
```

From the frontend, `fetch` works without any extra configuration:

```ts
await fetch("http://localhost:8900/api/sheet/demo", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ cells: { A1: "42" } }),
});
```

## API / Interface

**CORS policy** (set in `apps/api/main.py:44-50`):

| Setting             | Value                          |
|---------------------|--------------------------------|
| `allow_origins`     | `["http://localhost:5173"]`    |
| `allow_credentials` | `true`                         |
| `allow_methods`     | `["*"]`                        |
| `allow_headers`     | `["*"]`                        |

Behavior:

- `OPTIONS` preflight from `http://localhost:5173` → `200` with
  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:5173`,
  `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: *`,
  `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: <requested>`,
  `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, and `Vary: Origin`.
- `GET` / `POST` from `http://localhost:5173` → the existing response
  plus `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:5173` and
  `Vary: Origin`. Applies to every route, including
  `/api/sheet/{id}/export.csv`.
- Requests from other origins (e.g. `http://evil.example`) are rejected
  with `400 Disallowed CORS origin`; ACAO is not set.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-FIX-005 @ apps/api/main.py** — the API responds with correct
  CORS headers for cross-origin requests from `http://localhost:5173`.
  Preflight `OPTIONS` returns `200` with
  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:5173`, and real
  `POST` / `GET` responses carry the same header so the browser does
  not block them. Verified by `apps/api/tests/test_fix_005.py`
  (6 tests): preflight status, ACAO on preflight, allowed methods
  include `POST` / `GET`, ACAO on `POST` response, ACAO on `GET`
  response, and an end-to-end cross-origin `POST` whose body round-trips
  through the store.

## Limitations

- Only `http://localhost:5173` is allow-listed. A developer hitting
  `http://127.0.0.1:5173` (IP literal) will still be blocked — add that
  origin to `allow_origins` if you need it.
- The allow-list is hard-coded. There is no
  `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` environment override, so a production or
  staging deployment that talks to a different frontend origin needs a
  code change.
- `allow_methods=["*"]` is broader than the routes currently need
  (`GET` and `POST`); tightening it is a future hardening task.

SQLite journal mode set to WAL
The API's SQLite connection helper enables write-ahead logging so the sheets database tolerates concurrent readers during a writer without the default rollback journal's exclusive locks.

## Overview

`apps/api/main.py:_connect()` now runs `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`
immediately after opening each connection. WAL mode is recorded in the
SQLite database file header, so the setting persists across process
restarts and is picked up by every subsequent connection — including
raw `sqlite3.connect()` clients that never run the PRAGMA themselves.
This removes the writer-blocks-readers behavior of the default rollback
journal and lays the groundwork for heavier concurrent write load in
later features.

## Usage

Confirm WAL is active on a running instance by connecting to the DB
file and asking SQLite directly:

```bash
sqlite3 data/sheets.db 'PRAGMA journal_mode;'
# wal
```

Any fresh connection opened by the API's `_connect()` reports the same:

```python
from apps.api import main

conn = main._connect()
print(conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode;").fetchone()[0])
# wal
```

Because WAL mode is stored in the DB header, a bare `sqlite3` client
that never runs the PRAGMA still sees it:

```python
import sqlite3

conn = sqlite3.connect("data/sheets.db")
print(conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode;").fetchone()[0])
# wal
```

## API / Interface

`apps/api/main.py:28`:

```python
def _connect() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    path = _db_path()
    parent = Path(path).parent
    if str(parent) not in ("", "."):
        parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
    # ... CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sheets ...
    return conn
```

Observable effects:

- `PRAGMA journal_mode;` on any connection returns `wal`
  (case-insensitive).
- After the first `_connect()` against a fresh DB file, a `-wal` and
  `-shm` sidecar appear next to `sheets.db` while connections are open.
- Readers and writers no longer block each other on the `sheets` table
  under the volumes this API currently sees.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-FIX-007 @ apps/api/main.py:38** — SQLite is configured to use
  WAL (write-ahead logging) mode instead of the default rollback
  journal. `PRAGMA journal_mode;` returns `wal`, and the mode persists
  across restarts because SQLite stores it in the DB file header.
  Verified by `apps/api/tests/test_fix_007.py` (4 tests): `_connect()`
  reports `wal`; WAL persists across a fresh `sqlite3.connect()` that
  never ran the PRAGMA; the `POST` → `GET` round-trip still works with
  WAL active; and every one of several sequential `_connect()` calls
  reports `wal`.

## Limitations

- The PRAGMA runs on every `_connect()` call, which is cheap but
  redundant once the DB header is already `wal`. Not a correctness
  issue.
- WAL adds `sheets.db-wal` and `sheets.db-shm` sidecar files alongside
  `sheets.db`. Any backup or copy process must treat all three as a
  single unit.

## Overview

The `api` service in `docker-compose.yml` previously ran uvicorn with
`--reload`, a development-only flag that watches the filesystem and
restarts the worker on changes. That flag is now gone from the compose
command, so `docker compose up` runs a single long-lived uvicorn
process — the same process shape the Dockerfile `CMD` has always used.

## Usage

Boot the stack and check the actual process running as PID 1 in the
api container:

```bash
docker compose up -d --build api
docker exec sheets-clone-api cat /proc/1/cmdline | tr '\0' ' '
# python /usr/local/bin/uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8900
```

No `--reload` in the argv, so uvicorn will not fork a reloader parent
and will not restart on file edits under the bind-mounted `/app`.

## API / Interface

`docker-compose.yml:13` — the api service command:

```yaml
services:
  api:
    command: ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8900"]
```

`apps/api/Dockerfile:17` — the image default (unchanged; always
reload-free):

```dockerfile
CMD ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8900"]
```

Because both entrypoints now agree, removing the `command:` override
from compose would have the same effect — the Dockerfile `CMD` would
take over.

`VAL-*` id in the validation contract. The guard lives in
`apps/api/tests/test_fix_008.py` (3 tests):

Rapid keyboard typing no longer drops the first char
Multi-character cell edits typed back-to-back at native CDP speed now persist every character; Enter pressed mid-render commits and moves rather than reopening the editor.

Overview

Section titled “Overview”

Typing fast into the grid used to silently drop characters. With real keyboard input from page.keyboard.press(), around 1 in 9 multi-digit cells would persist only the second character (A18 ended up holding 8, A25 held 5, and so on). Three race conditions in apps/web/src/grid/Grid.tsx between the grid’s keydown handler and the inline editor’s mount cycle have been closed, so 100 back-to-back two-and-three-digit edits now round-trip correctly through the API and survive a reload.

Usage

Section titled “Usage”

There is nothing new to do — typing simply works at speed:

  1. Open /sheet/<any-id> and click cell A1.
  2. Type 1 Enter 2 Enter … all the way to 100 Enter as fast as the keyboard repeats.
  3. Reload. Every cell A1..A100 reads the value you typed.

The same regression test runs against the dev stack:

It drives 100 cells with page.keyboard.press() and no inter-key delays, asserts the rendered text for A1, A10, A18, A100, checks every value via GET /api/sheet/{id}, then reloads and re-checks.

API / Interface

Section titled “API / Interface”

No public API changed. The fix is three behavior changes in apps/web/src/grid/Grid.tsx:

1. Printable key arriving while already editing — append, don’t restart.

Previously the second key always called startEdit(sc, e.key), which overwrote editValue with just that one char.

2. Enter arriving while editingCell is set — commit and move down instead of restarting the editor.

The earlier code fell through to startEdit(sc), which reset editValue to the (still empty) cell value. The next iteration’s digits then filled the wrong cell and produced a consistent off-by-one across the run.

3. returnFocusToGrid is now synchronous.

The previous setTimeout(() => gridRef.current?.focus(), 0) left a window where document.body had focus and any keypress in that window was silently dropped.

F2 was also tightened to skip its startEdit call when an editor is already open, mirroring the new Enter handler.

A pagehide/beforeunload handler in usePersistence flushes the pending debounced save via navigator.sendBeacon, so values typed within the 500 ms debounce window survive a tab close or reload.

Overview

Section titled “Overview”

Persistence (F-011) writes are debounced 500 ms after every commit, and that timer was previously cleared on unmount with no flush. So typing 42 in A1, pressing Enter, and reloading or closing the tab inside that half-second silently lost the edit. usePersistence now registers pagehide and beforeunload listeners that flush any pending cells via navigator.sendBeacon, which the browser is required to deliver even as the page tears down.

Section titled “Usage”

Nothing for the user to do — the existing autosave just no longer drops the trailing edit. Concrete repro that previously failed:

  1. Open /sheet/persist-close-test and click A1.
  2. Press Enter, type 42, press Enter again to commit.
  3. Reload the tab immediately (well under 500 ms after the commit).
  4. After the reload, A1 reads 42. GET /api/sheet/persist-close-test returns {"cells": {"A1": "42"}}.

The regression test lives at apps/web/e2e/fix-010-unload-persist.spec.ts:

API / Interface

Section titled “API / Interface”

No public API change — usePersistence(sheetId) is still a single hook mounted by SheetPage. Two implementation additions in apps/web/src/hooks/usePersistence.ts:

1. A hasPendingRef flag tracks whether the debounce timer is armed. It flips true when the save effect schedules a setTimeout, and false either when the timer fires or when the unload handler flushes.

2. A pagehide + beforeunload listener flushes synchronously via sendBeacon if (and only if) a save is pending:

cellsRef and sheetIdRef are kept in sync on every render so the unload-time read is current. The listener is registered once for the lifetime of the component (empty dep array) and the closure reads the refs at call time. Both events are listened to because Safari fires pagehide but not beforeunload, and dedup is provided by the hasPendingRef guard — only one POST goes out even if both fire.

The beacon payload format matches the regular saveSheet POST body ({"cells": {…}}), so the existing POST /api/sheet/{id} endpoint handles it without change.

Backup uses SQLite's online-backup API instead of a raw file copy

apps/api/backup.py now snapshots the database via sqlite3.Connection.backup(), which is consistent under concurrent writers and WAL journal mode — no more torn or incomplete snapshots from raw file copies.

## Overview

`apps/api/backup.py` previously called `shutil.copy2(source_db, dest)` to
produce its snapshot. That is a plain byte-for-byte file copy and is
unsafe while the database is being written: pages still in the rollback
journal or `-wal` sidecar may be missing from the destination, leaving a
silently corrupt backup. `run_backup()` now opens both ends with
`sqlite3.connect` and copies through `sqlite3.Connection.backup()`,
SQLite's Online Backup API, which holds the appropriate read locks for a
transactionally-consistent snapshot.

## Usage

The CLI surface is unchanged — same arguments, same exit codes:

```bash
python apps/api/backup.py sheets.db /var/backups/sheets
# INFO Backup written to /var/backups/sheets/sheets.db
# OK: /var/backups/sheets/sheets.db
echo $?
# 0
```

The behavioural change is observable by running the CLI against a
database that is being actively written. The destination now passes
`PRAGMA integrity_check`:

```bash
python apps/api/backup.py sheets.db /var/backups/sheets
sqlite3 /var/backups/sheets/sheets.db 'PRAGMA integrity_check;'
# ok
```

## API / Interface

`run_backup(source_db, backup_dir, *, disk_threshold=0.80) -> Path` keeps
the same signature, the same disk-space precheck, and the same
`DiskSpaceError` failure mode from F-FIX-004. The copy step in
`apps/api/backup.py:62-69` now reads:

```python
dest = backup_dir / source_db.name
# Use SQLite's online-backup API: safe under concurrent writers and WAL mode.
src_conn = sqlite3.connect(str(source_db))
dst_conn = sqlite3.connect(str(dest))
try:
    src_conn.backup(dst_conn)
finally:
    dst_conn.close()
    src_conn.close()
```

Both connections are closed in a `finally` so file handles are released
even if `backup()` raises mid-copy. No `-wal` / `-shm` sidecars remain
in `backup_dir` after the call returns — the destination is a single
self-contained `.db` file.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-FIX-011 @ apps/api/backup.py:61** — backup produces a valid
  snapshot under concurrent writes. Verified by
  `apps/api/tests/test_fix_011.py` (5 tests): the destination passes
  `PRAGMA integrity_check = 'ok'`, contains at least the seeded row,
  still passes integrity-check when a concurrent writer thread is
  hammering the source DB every 10 ms during the backup, the snapshot
  taken under that load is non-empty, and `shutil.copy2` is never
  invoked by `run_backup()`.

## Limitations

- **Nonexistent source path is not an error.** `sqlite3.connect()`
  creates a missing file before `backup()` runs, so calling
  `run_backup("does-not-exist.db", ...)` silently fabricates an empty
  source DB and reports success. Tracked as a follow-up.
- **Read lock held for the full copy.** `Connection.backup()` defaults
  to `pages=-1` (copy in one shot), which keeps a read lock for the
  duration. Latency grows with database size; large DBs may want to
  pass `pages=N` and a `progress` callback to checkpoint between
  chunks.
- **Backup module is still not scheduled.** Like F-FIX-004 noted, no
  cron, compose service, or FastAPI endpoint invokes `run_backup()` —
  operators must call it manually.

  `DiskSpaceError`; this fix replaces the copy step it left behind.
- [F-002](/features/F-002/) — FastAPI + SQLite sheet store whose

Backup runs automatically and is reachable from the app
backup.py is now wired into FastAPI as a lifespan-managed scheduler, exposed as POST /api/backup, and configured by docker-compose so snapshots land on the api-data volume with timestamped filenames.

## Overview

`apps/api/backup.py` previously existed as a standalone script that
nothing in the deployed system invoked — no FastAPI route, no cron, no
compose service. It now runs automatically: on application startup the
FastAPI lifespan starts a background coroutine that calls `run_backup()`
every `BACKUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (default 3600s). A `POST /api/backup`
endpoint also lets operators trigger a snapshot on demand. Snapshot
filenames now embed an ISO-style timestamp so successive runs no longer
overwrite each other.

## Usage

Trigger a backup manually against a running api container:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8900/api/backup
# {"status":"ok","dest":"/data/backups/sheets_20260425_035811.db"}
```

The same endpoint is used by external monitors / cron — the response
body names the artifact path so callers can verify it landed.

The scheduled loop runs without intervention; check for new files in the
configured backup directory:

```bash
docker compose exec api ls -1 /data/backups
# sheets_20260425_035811.db
# sheets_20260425_045811.db
```

To shorten the interval for testing, set `BACKUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`:

```bash
BACKUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS=60 docker compose up api
```

## API / Interface

**`POST /api/backup`** (apps/api/main.py:108) — triggers `run_backup()`
synchronously against the configured paths. Responses:

- `200 {"status": "ok", "dest": "<path>"}` on success.
- `507 Insufficient Storage` when `DiskSpaceError` is raised
  (target disk is more than 80% full — see [F-FIX-004](/features/F-FIX-004/)).
- `500` on other `OSError` — message contains the underlying error.

**Environment variables** read by `apps/api/main.py`:

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `BACKUP_DIR` | `./backups` | Directory `run_backup` writes snapshots into. `docker-compose.yml` sets this to `/data/backups`, which lives on the `api-data` named volume. |
| `BACKUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | `3600` | Sleep between scheduled backup runs in the lifespan loop. |
| `SHEETS_DB_PATH` | `./sheets.db` | Source database that gets snapshotted. |

**Snapshot filename** (apps/api/backup.py:62) —
`{source_stem}_{YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS}.db`. With the default
`SHEETS_DB_PATH=/data/sheets.db`, files appear as
`sheets_20260425_035811.db`. Successive backups no longer collide.

**Lifespan integration** (apps/api/main.py:34-49) — `_backup_loop()` is
spawned via `asyncio.create_task` from the `@asynccontextmanager
lifespan(app)` handler and cancelled cleanly on shutdown. Failures
inside the loop are logged at `ERROR` level (`DiskSpaceError` is logged

Formula normalizer preserves quoted string literals
normalizeFormula now skips over "..."  segments so that TRUE / FALSE / CONCAT appearing inside string literals are no longer rewritten before being handed to HyperFormula.

## Overview

The `CONCAT → CONCATENATE` and bare-`TRUE`/`FALSE` → `TRUE()`/`FALSE()`
rewrites that `normalizeFormula` performs on every formula are now
applied **only outside quoted string literals**. Previously the two
global regexes ran across the whole formula, so a string argument like
`"the CONCAT word"` was silently mutated to `"the CONCATENATE word"`
before HyperFormula ever saw it. Users typing such strings now see them
render exactly as written.

## Usage

Open any sheet and enter the following — each cell renders the literal
string the user typed, not a rewritten variant:

```
A1 = =CONCAT("the CONCAT word","!")           → the CONCAT word!
B1 = =CONCATENATE("It is TRUE that","...")    → It is TRUE that...
C1 = =IF(1>0,"TRUE result","FALSE result")    → TRUE result
```

Tokens outside the quotes are still rewritten, so the original
HyperFormula-compatibility shims keep working:

```
D1 = =CONCAT("a","b")     → ab        (CONCAT → CONCATENATE outside the strings)
E1 = =AND(TRUE,FALSE)     → FALSE     (bare TRUE/FALSE → TRUE()/FALSE())
F1 = =IF(TRUE,"x","y")    → x
```

Excel-style escaped quotes (`""` inside a string) are honored — the
tokenizer treats them as a literal `"` and keeps consuming the string:

```
G1 = =CONCAT("she said ""CONCAT""","!")  → she said "CONCAT"!
```

## API / Interface

No public API change. The fix is internal to
`normalizeFormula(formula: string): string` in
`apps/web/src/engine/formulaEngine.ts:29`. The two-line regex
implementation was replaced with a character-level tokenizer that
alternates between two states:

- **Inside a quoted literal** (entered on `"`): consume characters
  unchanged until an unescaped closing `"`. A doubled `""` is treated as
  an escaped quote and consumption continues.
- **Outside any literal**: collect the run up to the next `"` (or end
  of formula) and apply the original rewrites:
  `\b(TRUE|FALSE)\b(?!\s*\()` → `$1()` and `\bCONCAT\b` → `CONCATENATE`,
  both case-insensitive.

The pieces are concatenated and returned. All callers
(`parseRawValue` in `apps/web/src/engine/formulaEngine.ts:67` and
anything else that round-trips a formula through the engine) get the
new behavior automatically.

## Claims satisfied

- **VAL-FIX-013** (`apps/web/src/engine/formulaEngine.ts:21`) —
  `normalizeFormula` preserves quoted string literals. Verified by
  three Playwright assertions in
  `apps/web/e2e/fix-013-normalize-formula.spec.ts`:
  `=CONCAT("the CONCAT word","!")` renders `the CONCAT word!`,
  `=CONCATENATE("It is TRUE that","...")` renders `It is TRUE that...`,
  and `=IF(1>0,"TRUE result","FALSE result")` renders `TRUE result`.

## Limitations

- Only Excel-style double-quoted (`"..."`) string literals are
  recognized. HyperFormula does not accept single-quoted string
  literals in formulas, so this is not a regression — but if a future
  feature introduces another quoting form, the tokenizer will need to
  learn it.
- Replacements still operate on raw text outside strings rather than on
  a real parse tree, so contrived identifiers like a hypothetical sheet
  or named-range called `CONCAT` would still be rewritten. No such
  names exist in the current product.
