_connect() now executes db/schema.sql, so deployed DBs get the customers table and idx_customers_email — not just pytest fixtures.

## Overview

The API's per-connection setup now applies the full `apps/api/db/schema.sql`
script instead of inlining a sheets-only `CREATE TABLE`. Deployed instances
of the service therefore get every object the schema declares — the
`sheets` and `customers` tables and the `idx_customers_email` index — on
the first connection to a fresh database file. Previously the customers
table existed only in pytest's `tmp_path` databases (where the test
fixture explicitly applied the schema), so the F-FIX-003 index lived
nowhere a real client could reach.

## Usage

Start the API against an empty database directory and connect with the
SQLite CLI; both tables and the index are present after the first
request:

```bash
SHEETS_DB_PATH=/tmp/sheets-clone-fresh.db uvicorn apps.api.main:app &
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8900/api/sheet/probe > /dev/null

sqlite3 /tmp/sheets-clone-fresh.db \
  "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type IN ('table','index') ORDER BY name;"
# customers
# idx_customers_email
# sheets
# sqlite_autoindex_customers_1

sqlite3 /tmp/sheets-clone-fresh.db "PRAGMA index_info(idx_customers_email);"
# 0|1|email
```

Existing databases that predate the `updated_at` column on `sheets` are
migrated lazily on connect: `_connect()` checks `PRAGMA table_info` and
runs `ALTER TABLE sheets ADD COLUMN updated_at TEXT` plus a backfill if
the column is missing.

## API / Interface

**`apps/api/main.py:_connect()`** — every SQLite connection opens like
this:

```python
conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
schema_path = Path(__file__).parent / "db" / "schema.sql"
conn.executescript(schema_path.read_text())
# lazy backfill for pre-updated_at sheets DBs
cur = conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(sheets)")
cols = {row[1] for row in cur.fetchall()}
if "updated_at" not in cols:
    conn.execute("ALTER TABLE sheets ADD COLUMN updated_at TEXT")
    conn.execute("UPDATE sheets SET updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE updated_at IS NULL")
    conn.commit()
```

`PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` runs first because `executescript()` issues an
implicit `COMMIT` and the journal mode is connection-scoped.

tables. The `sheets` table definition was extended with the `updated_at`
column so the file matches the runtime schema:

```sql
    id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    cells      TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
```

ASCII `filename=` form and the RFC 5987 `filename*=UTF-8''…` form, so the

```bash
  -d '{"cells": {"A1": "hello"}}'

# content-disposition: attachment; filename="%ED%95%9C%EA%B8%80sheet.csv"; filename*=UTF-8''%ED%95%9C%EA%B8%80sheet.csv
```

Dot-delimited strings like 1.2.3 stay as text
parseRawValue now detects N.N.N+ patterns and routes them through HyperFormula as literal strings, so semver-like inputs no longer silently become date serials.

## Overview

Typing `1.2.3` into a cell used to render `37653` with
`data-cell-type="number"` — HyperFormula was tokenising the value as
day=1, month=2, year=3 and returning the date serial for 1 Feb 2003.
Semver, IP-fragment, and similar dotted inputs were silently destroyed.
The cell now displays the original string (`1.2.3`), the type is no
longer `number`, and `F2` re-opens the editor with exactly what the
user typed. The Excel-style `'1.2.3` text-prefix workaround still
works but is no longer necessary.

## Usage

Open any sheet and enter a dotted version string — it round-trips as
text:

1. Click `A1`, type `1.2.3`, press `Enter`. Cell renders `1.2.3` (not
   `37653`); `data-cell-type` is no longer `number`.
2. Click `A1` again, press `F2`. The editor shows `1.2.3` — the
   original input, not a date serial or `="1.2.3"`.
3. Reload the page. `A1` still reads `1.2.3` (the raw string is what's
   persisted).

The same applies to any `N.N.N` or longer chain — `2.0.1`, `3.4.5`,
`10.2.0.4`, etc. Pure two-segment numerics like `1.5` are still parsed
as numbers (`1.5`, right-aligned), since they're unambiguous floats.

## API / Interface

No public API change. The fix is in
`apps/web/src/engine/formulaEngine.ts:parseRawValue` — a single
guard added before the value is handed to HyperFormula:

```ts
// Matches version-like strings with two or more dots (e.g. "1.2.3", "2.0.1").
const SEMVER_LIKE_RE = /^\d+(\.\d+){2,}$/;

function parseRawValue(raw: string): RawCellContent {
  if (raw.startsWith("=")) return normalizeFormula(raw);
  const upper = raw.trim().toUpperCase();
  if (upper === "TRUE") return true;
  if (upper === "FALSE") return false;
  const trimmed = raw.trim();
  if (trimmed !== "" && !isNaN(Number(trimmed))) return Number(trimmed);
  // Wrap N.N.N+ patterns as a formula literal so HyperFormula evaluates
  // them to the exact string without attempting date inference.
  if (SEMVER_LIKE_RE.test(trimmed)) return `="${trimmed}"`;
```

Overview

Section titled “Overview”

Typing 1.2.3 into a cell used to render 37653 with data-cell-type="number" — HyperFormula was tokenising the value as day=1, month=2, year=3 and returning the date serial for 1 Feb 2003. The Excel-style '1.2.3 text-prefix workaround still works but is no longer necessary.
